content: The Duke University Health System integrates the Duke University School of Medicine, the Duke University School of Nursing, the Duke Clinic, and its affiliated hospitals into a comprehensive network dedicated to research, clinical care, and education. Duke University Hospital In 1925, James B. Duke allocated $4 million to establish the Duke University School of Medicine, the Duke University School of Nursing, and the Duke University Hospital with the goal of advancing healthcare in the Carolinas and across the United States. Construction of the hospital and medical school began in 1927, and the hospital officially opened to patients on July 21, 1930. On its first day, 17 of the hospital's 400 beds were occupied. In 1936, Dr. Julian Deryl Hart, a surgeon at Duke, introduced the use of ultraviolet lights in operating rooms to eliminate airborne pathogens. In 1956, Duke surgeons pioneered the use of systemic hypothermia during cardiac surgery, a technique that has since become a global standard of care. The Medical School and Hospital were renamed the Duke University Medical Center in 1957. The first African American student was admitted to the Duke University School of Medicine in 1963. In 1969, groundbreaking studies were conducted at Duke to evaluate human capabilities to function and work under pressures equivalent to a 1,000-foot deep-sea dive. During the 1990s, Duke geneticists developed a three-minute test capable of screening newborns for over 30 metabolic diseases simultaneously, a test now widely used across the United States. In 1992, Duke performed its first lung transplant and heart-lung transplant. Duke Children’s Hospital and Health Center Duke Children’s Hospital & Health Center specializes in providing healthcare for children from birth through young adulthood. The hospital includes a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). The McGovern-Davison Children’s Health Center, located within the hospital, offers outpatient care across more than 28 pediatric medical and surgical specialties. Additionally, Duke Children’s provides primary care services at multiple locations within Durham County. The Duke Children’s Miracle Network raises unrestricted funds to support the hospital’s research, clinical care, and family support programs through the Children’s Miracle Network. Durham Regional Hospital Durham Regional Hospital offers inpatient, outpatient, surgical, and emergency care. It features a Level II intensive care nursery, the Durham Regional Rehabilitation Institute, and the Davis Ambulatory Surgical Center. Newborn care at this hospital is provided by physicians from Duke Children’s Hospital. Historically, the hospital was known as Lincoln Hospital and Watts Hospital. Duke Raleigh Hospital Duke Raleigh Hospital (DRH) has been part of the Duke University Health System since 1998. Originally named Mary Elizabeth Hospital when it opened in 1914, it was later renamed Raleigh Community Hospital and relocated to its current site on Wake Forest Road in 1978. The hospital has 186 beds and a medical staff of over 500 physicians. Newborn care at Duke Raleigh Hospital is provided by Duke Children’s Hospital physicians, and Duke Children’s Consultative Services of Raleigh also operates at this location. In 2004, the hospital mistakenly used hydraulic fluid instead of detergents to sterilize surgical instruments. As a result, over 3,800 patients were notified of their potential exposure to harmful chemicals.
